liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **New Minglewood Blues** (2 reviews): Reviewer hears a squealing slide guitar in Minglewood and wonders if Bobby is learning slide on the fly; Reviewer hears some beautiful slide guitar; the band is in top form [19][20]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 other source): After CC Rider a false start fizzles out; there's tuning, then Terrapin Station begins [1]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-06-13.144767.fob.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 172 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd80-06-13.akg.clugston.7196.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 159 min; rated 4.55/5 by 11 [4]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds very good and immersive, with a PA hiccup during Minglewood; Reviewer, usually not an audience-tape fan, was pleased with how this recording sounds; Fairly high-quality audience tape, slightly trebly with little bass, needing some EQ [9][13][15][18]
- **gd1980-06-13.155744.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 161 min [5]
- **gd1980-06-13.fob.sonyecm990.morris.100259.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 162 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [8]. Said about its sound: Reviewer considers the Bob Morris recording very good in quality [16]

## Around the show

- Garcia's guitar playing was especially expressive and busy this night [9]
- Reviewer stood on the wall in front of Phil, stage right; tickets were $10 and scalped for up to $50 [10]
- Weir broke a string during the show; reviewer attended both nights and stood by the wall or fence [11]
- Reviewer's second show; Jerry's fingers were very talkative, making it their favorite Dead concert out of dozens [12]
- Jams are wild and the band makes frequent mistakes [15]
- The crowd reacts audibly to something on the recording [19]
- Reviewer ranks it best show of 1980, a straightforward two-set electric show unlike the October acoustic shows [9]
- The previous year's show filled the 15,000-seat Coliseum; this year's setup was a roughly 5,000-seat arena with scarce tickets [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-06-13.144767.fob.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics (DFC, mounted on pole 35' from stage) > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII) [1]. Also: A 0:07 patch in Wharf Rat comes from the AKG SE-5 with CE-1 capsules source, shnid 7196 [1]
- **gd80-06-13.akg.clugston.7196.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: AKG SE-5 mics w/CE-1 cardioid capsules [4]. Also: Master audience cassette: AKG SE-5 mics with CE-1 cardioid capsules, Sony TC-D5, then DAT, then CDR; shn by Scott Clugston [4]
- **gd1980-06-13.155744.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; transferred by Scott Wiseman and Scott Clugston; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG SE-5E mics with CE-1 cardioid capsules > Sony TC-D5 (TDK SA 90, except Sugar Magnolia and Alabama Getaway-Maxell… [5]. Also: Severson's Nakamichi 700 source supplies some crowd, the start of Don't Ease Me In, and an 0:08 patch in the Wharf Rat to Sugar Magnolia transition [5]
- **gd1980-06-13.fob.sonyecm990.morris.100259.flac16**: taped by Bob Morris; source: (FOB) Sony ECM-990 stereo mic > Cassette Master (Marantz Superscope CD320/Maxell UDXLII except: d3t03-d3t08 UDXLI) [8]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Peter Simon Grateful Dead: [1980-06-13 Seattle Center Coliseum, Seattle, WA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1980-06-13-seattle-center-coliseum-seattle-wa-usa/) [22]
